text: alex: Heads-up — int4-v2p1 preliminary canary shows improved cost and median latency but a small quality regression on long-doc slices. Proposal: stepped promotion with 3-stage ramp (0.5%, 2%, 10%) and an automatic failsafe that falls back to v2 when any trigger fires within a 30m window: (1) absolute MRR drop >= 0.8% vs baseline, (2) hallucination rate delta >= +1.5 percentage points, (3) long-doc truncation/error rate >= 0.4%, (4) p99 latency degradation > 20% (p95 > 15% as secondary). Will sketch config below.
text_2: maria: Can you paste the AB numbers and sample sizes? Also we should decide whether the trigger window is sliding or fixed buckets. :thinking:
text_3: tariq: quick snapshot from last 2h AB run (long-doc slice, >500 tokens): baseline v2 MRR=0.652, candidate int4-v2p1 MRR=0.641 (Δ -0.011 absolute = -1.69% relative). Hallucination proxy (LM-qa mismatch): baseline=2.1%, candidate=3.6% (+1.5pp). Latency: p50 baseline 95ms vs candidate 88ms, p95 baseline 210ms vs candidate 190ms, p99 baseline 420ms vs candidate 520ms (+24%). Sampled n=4,200 long-doc queries.
text_5: ingrid: LGTM. Two tweaks: (1) add a short exponential backoff to avoid flip-flopping (cooldown + progressive unstuck), (2) require Bayesian smoothing for small slices (n < 500) so rare spikes don't trigger. Also include kv-warmup probe before next ramp.
text_6: maria: +1 to persistence + Bayesian smoothing. Also prefer 'sliding' window semantics so we catch gradual drift rather than bucket artifacts.
